qualifying_findings.title: 9Router public LLM API can trust spoofed local-client headers
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: 9Router before 0.5.6 can classify a remote request as local when a deployment lets traffic reach Next.js without the sanitizing custom-server.js wrapper. The vulnerable guard trusts a client-supplied X-9r-Real-Ip value, allowing an unauthenticated caller to set 127.0.0.1 and bypass API-key validation for public LLM API routes such as GET /api/v1/models.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary CVE record with GitHub security advisory, patch commit, and release reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: decolua/9router versions before 0.5.6; public LLM API authorization path; src/dashboardGuard.js local-request decision.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An AI router's model API boundary can be crossed without an API key when deployment topology exposes the unsanitized Next.js route, turning network/header trust into model-access authorization.

qualifying_findings.title: FastGPT safe Axios guard permits DNS-rebinding SSRF
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: FastGPT before 4.15.2 checks a hostname with isInternalAddress() in its safe Axios interceptor before a later HTTP connection performs a separate DNS lookup. An authenticated attacker controlling a hostname can pass the check with a public address and then rebind to loopback, private, link-local, or metadata addresses during connection.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary CVE record with GitHub security advisory, pull request, patch commit, and release reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: labring/FastGPT versions before 4.15.2; packages/service/common/api/axios.ts safe Axios outbound-request guard.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Knowledge-base AI applications often fetch user-controlled URLs for retrieval, plugin, or workflow actions; a DNS-rebinding SSRF bypass can expose cloud metadata, private services, or internal endpoints through an AI application backend.

qualifying_findings.title: vLLM NIXL prefix caching can terminate decode workers
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: vLLM through 0.29.0 fails to validate block counts correctly in the NIXL connector's prefix caching path for multi-prompt completion requests in prefill/decode disaggregated deployments. Attackers can submit prompts of varying lengths to trigger an assertion failure in NixlBaseConnectorWorker._apply_prefix_caching, terminating the decode worker until restart.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE Services record with VulnCheck advisory and upstream code/pull-request references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: vllm-project/vllm 0.29.0 and earlier; NIXL KV-transfer connector; prefill/decode disaggregated deployments using prefix caching.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Shared model-serving infrastructure can be made unavailable through model-runtime request shape rather than conventional network overload, making inference capacity and release gates part of AI security assurance.

qualifying_findings.title: vLLM Mooncake transfer IDs can leak GPU KV cache blocks
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: vLLM Mooncake connector through 0.29.0 does not properly manage GPU KV cache block ownership when concurrent child requests share a transfer ID in prefill/decode disaggregated deployments. Attackers can send multi-prompt completion requests that leave orphaned KV cache blocks, exhausting GPU memory until restart.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE Services record with VulnCheck advisory and upstream code/pull-request references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: vllm-project/vllm 0.29.0 and earlier; Mooncake KV-transfer connector; GPU KV cache ownership in prefill/decode disaggregated deployments.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: A model-serving connector can lose GPU memory through attacker-shaped inference requests, creating an availability and capacity-isolation risk for hosted LLM deployments.

qualifying_findings.title: MCP Atlassian publishes a 0.22.0 advisory cluster for SSRF, auth, token, filter, and file-read boundaries

related_cves.title: Incomplete fix for CVE-2026-27826: DNS rebinding bypasses SSRF validation because the validated IP is not pinned
ENABLED_TOOLS and TOOLSETS authorization bypass allows direct invocation of hidden tools
HTTP transport authentication bypass accepts any non-empty Atlassian opaque token
OAuth fallback token storage writes plaintext access and refresh tokens with group-readable permissions
JIRA_PROJECTS_FILTER and CONFLUENCE_SPACES_FILTER allow forbidden-project content exfiltration
Caller-supplied search filters can replace administrator-configured Jira and Confluence allowlists
Confluence upload_attachment accepts arbitrary server-local file paths
Confluence and Jira upload_attachment implementations permit arbitrary local file read
SSRF redirect protection is missing for basic-auth and OAuth branches
Header-based authentication flow permits DNS-rebinding SSRF
Header-supplied Jira and Confluence URLs bypass SSRF validation
Attachment upload tools trust caller-controlled server-local file paths

qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: MCP Atlassian versions before 0.22.0 published a same-window advisory cluster covering SSRF validation gaps, DNS rebinding, toolset authorization bypass, HTTP transport authentication bypass, plaintext OAuth fallback token storage, Jira/Confluence filter bypasses, and arbitrary local file read through attachment upload tools. The shared patch reference is PR 1448 and commit b041733473f95119dd539542a43c280737a8e460.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: multiple primary CVE Services records with GitHub security advisory references, shared patch PR, commit, and release boundary
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: sooperset/mcp-atlassian versions before 0.22.0; Jira and Confluence MCP transports, fetchers, auth headers, tool dispatch, OAuth token storage, search filters, and attachment upload tools.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An MCP server often sits between agents and high-value Jira/Confluence workspaces. This cluster crosses authentication, delegated-tool authorization, data allowlists, SSRF protections, local file reads, and credential storage, so an agent or attacker-controlled MCP caller could exceed intended authority and expose workspace or host data.
